method: The script is trimmed, its words are the whitespace-separated tokens, and every line is wrapped greedily: words join the current line while the line plus one space plus the next word stays within the character width, otherwise the line breaks before that word, and a word longer than the width is placed alone on its own line and counted as an overlong word. A blank line becomes one empty line, which occupies one line height, and runs of spaces or tabs inside a paragraph collapse to a single space. Script height = wrapped lines x line height. Read time = 60 x words / reading rate in words per minute. Scroll speed = script height / read time, equivalently height x rate / (60 x words); one screen of text passes in screen height / speed, and the lines fully on screen are floor(screen height / line height). With a target slot of S seconds the required rate is 60 x words / S, the required speed is height / S, and the current pace over-runs the slot by read time - S. A monospaced, constant-speed scroll of the whole script height during the read is assumed: character widths, paragraph spacing beyond the empty lines, the lines that remain below the reading line, prompter speed ramps and the prompter's own font metrics are not modelled. Bounds are a script of up to 20,000 characters, 8-200 characters per line, 8-400 px line height, 120-4320 px screen height, 40-400 words per minute and a 5-7200 s slot, and the screen must be at least one line tall. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads, accounts or network access.
